incidents.title: Fideuram chairman tricked by cloned voice and fake CEO messages into EUR 95M transfers
incidents.outcome: About EUR 95M sent overseas; about EUR 53M recovered, EUR 36M converted to crypto and untraced.
incidents.confidenceReason: Gulf News relays Reuters relaying 'two people familiar with the matter': 'According to the sources cited by Reuters, AI technology was used to replicate the lawyer's voice'. Victim 'declined to comment'; no investigator or prosecutor statement on AI in the source.
incidents.summary: A WhatsApp message posing as the Intesa CEO about a secret acquisition was followed by a call in the cloned voice of a known lawyer. Milan prosecutors and Eurojust are investigating; the disclosure date is approximate.
incidents.quote: AI voice-cloning scammers stole €95m from Italian bank Fideuram by impersonating top executives and a lawyer, exposing rising deepfake risks in finance.

harness.note: AI used as an assistant, no agent harness

sources.title: AI Voice-Cloning Scam Hits Italian Bank
Fideuram fraud: Italian prosecutors link similar scams using voice cloning (ANSA)

incidents.title: Russian-speaking actor uses commercial generative AI services to compromise over 600 FortiGate devices in 55 countries
incidents.targets: More than 600 FortiGate devices across over 55 countries; some Active Directory environments
incidents.outcome: More than 600 FortiGate devices in 55 countries were accessed through exposed management interfaces and weak credentials.
incidents.confidenceReason: Amazon Threat Intelligence, which investigated the activity, states the actor used several commercial generative AI services.
incidents.summary: A low-skilled, Russian-speaking, financially motivated actor used multiple commercial generative AI services to plan and tool a campaign that accessed more than 600 FortiGate devices without exploiting any software flaw. Activity ran 11 January to 18 February 2026.
incidents.quote: Amazon Threat Intelligence observed a Russian-speaking financially motivated threat actor leveraging multiple commercial generative AI services to compromise over 600 FortiGate devices across more than 55 countries from January 11 to February 18, 2026.

incidents.title: Slopoly: likely AI-generated PowerShell backdoor in Hive0163 ransomware attack
incidents.targets: Enterprise victim of ClickFix-initiated ransomware intrusion
incidents.outcome: Backdoor gave persistent access for more than a week during a ransomware engagement.
incidents.confidenceReason: IBM X-Force infers AI generation from comments and code style and could not identify the model.
incidents.summary: X-Force found a technically mediocre PowerShell C2 client during a live ransomware response, with clear variable names and detailed comments that looked machine-written. They say it shows AI speeding up malware development.
incidents.quote: IBM X-Force discovered a likely AI-generated novel malware which we are dubbing “Slopoly,” used during a ransomware attack.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only IBM X-Force has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

harness.note: AI used as assistant or tool, not as an agent harness

sources.title: A Slopoly start to AI-enhanced ransomware attacks

incidents.title: UAT-10147 uses PentestGPT, DeepAudit and AI-written scripts against web servers
incidents.targets: About 170,000 target URLs; Windows and Linux web servers worldwide (Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, Vietnam seen)
incidents.outcome: Mass exploitation, SPECTRE backdoor deployment, SEO fraud and data theft.
incidents.confidenceReason: Talos recovered the tools and AI-generated scripts from an exposed attacker download server.
incidents.summary: Talos found the actor running PentestGPT and DeepAudit to scan servers and run matching exploits, plus AI-generated Python scripts automating an ASP.NET ViewState RCE chain. A companion report says AI helped write a Linux rootkit.
incidents.quote: The actor employed a mixture of open-source offensive frameworks, including Metasploit, ysoserial, PentestGPT, DeepAudit, and multiple privilege escalation exploits to automate intrusion operations and establish persistence.

harness.note: Open-source offensive frameworks scanned servers and ran matching exploits; underlying LLM not named
